answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in a vault ledger and posts a cipher-sealed provenance chain: every output cites a distinct onyx artifact, sealed with its own key, and the vault stamps each link. An auditor replays the chain to its onyx root; a reused or broken link burns the bond and voids the payment. The k-th fake identity needs a fresh chain, paying 70 bond plus 25 artifact fee plus 5(k-1) replay fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 2,522,500 in fees. An artifact-rental ring fails because a rented seal is key-bound and replay exposes the break. An honest identity pays 95 once.
